findings.evidence: Row text: 'Every unit of work must be retried three times before it is reported as failed.' origin=sourced, sources=['F-b1-02'], quote='The core imports interfaces, never implementations'. python3 tools/kb.py show F-b1-02 returns text '1. **Every external dependency sits behind a capability interface.** The core imports interfaces, never implementations.' -- design rule 1, about the interface/implementation boundary. The quote is a verbatim substring of F-b1-02 (passes a naive check) but F-b1-02 says nothing about retries, retry counts, or failure reporting; no other source is cited. The claim is invented and dressed in an unrelated real quote, the same fabrication pattern ceremony 59 found in build-evidence-record (R59A-001). It is also the sole cap-policy row citing F-b1-02, and agentic-stack states design rule 1 under the identical quote (validator: 'cap-policy: restates F-b1-02 under the same quote as agentic-stack, build-adapter-pair, without naming it'), so even read charitably as a mangled restatement it names neither the rule it actually quotes nor the source skill.
findings.fix: Delete the row; nothing in cap-policy's cited ids or builds_on skills supports a three-retry rule, and cap-policy's own contract (deterministic allow/deny before spend) has no retry semantics to state.

findings.evidence: Row: 'A criterion nothing can fail is not a criterion, so every gate carries a breakage.' origin=sourced, sources=['F-part-c-04'], quote='A criterion nothing can fail is not a criterion'. cap-policy's builds_on list includes both agentic-stack and build-definition-of-done, and both already state this exact fact under the identical quote (F-part-c-04: 'A criterion nothing can fail is not a criterion.'). python3 tools/validate_skills.py --only cap-policy: 'restates F-part-c-04 under the same quote as agentic-stack, build-skill-authoring, without naming it'. The row names neither owning skill.
findings.fix: Prefix the row with 'agentic-stack and build-definition-of-done already state this (F-part-c-04)' and keep only cap-policy's own consequence (every gate carries a breakage) as the added content.

findings.evidence: The Decision shape's name field is 'Decision (shape governed by the recorded standard; what crosses the interface, whichever engine served it)', sources=['F-b4-04','F-b4-07'], quote='Typed and machine-readable. Never parsed from prose' (F-b4-07). Neither cap-errors nor agentic-stack, both of which state this exact fact under the identical quote and both of which are in cap-policy's builds_on list, is named anywhere in this row (the shape has no prose field besides 'name', and 'name' does not mention either skill). instructions[6] and contract.invariants[8] cite the same fact and do name cap-errors, so the omission is local to this row rather than a whole-skill issue.
findings.fix: Add a clause to the shape's name/description naming cap-errors as the owner of the typed-failure fact, e.g. 'failure shape owned by cap-errors (F-b4-07)'.

findings.evidence: action: 'Adopt the two recorded standards whole and design no actor model of our own...' why: '...agentic-stack states design rule 2 (F-b1-03); what this adds is that Identity is the one capability whose interface has to satisfy two standards at once...' origin=sourced, sources=['F-b3-14','F-b1-03'], quote='OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange · workload identity'. The restatement (design rule 2) is properly cited and names agentic-stack, but the extension clause after 'what this adds' -- the claim that Identity is uniquely the one capability needing two standards at once -- carries no citation of its own and the row is not marked proposed, matching this repo's own MECH-2 pattern (build-ceremony best_practices[3]/quality ceremony 01). python3 tools/validate_skills.py --only cap-identity confirms: 'sourced row restates and extends ("what this adds") without saying proposed'.
findings.fix: Mark the 'what this adds' clause proposed, or cite a fact establishing that no other capability's interface names two governing standards.

summary: Reviewed all 13 skills' skill.json data and rendered SKILL.md against the standard: python3 tools/kb.py show for every distinct cited id; a mechanical script resolving every sourced/claimed/measured row's cited sources and confirming its quote is a verbatim substring of at least one (0 misquotes of that kind found across 328 quoted rows, including adapters[] and definition_of_done rows which schema-require a quote); python3 tools/validate_skills.py --only per skill (0 errors on all 13; warnings only -- one 'not a pure shell command' DoD note per skill with a claimed-status criterion, and restate-and-extend warnings on 9 of the 13); and live re-execution of every definition_of_done whose criterion names a runnable tool: bash harness/{idempotency,identity,containment,memory,policy,gateway}/test.sh all reproduced their recorded clean pass exactly (16, 46, 25, 23, 38, 25 checks respectively, 0 failed), matching each skill's measured_run block; every claimed-status DoD (cap-idempotency, cap-identity, cap-isolation, cap-mandate-broker, cap-mandate-broker-implement, cap-memory, cap-model-access, cap-policy) names a tool confirmed absent from the tree, consistent with its status, and cap-mandate-broker-implement discloses the missing-harness gap by name (STATUS row 60). One high-severity fabricated claim found: cap-policy best_practices[5] asserts a three-retry rule under a verbatim but topically unrelated quote from F-b1-02 (design rule 1, about interfaces vs implementations), the same fabrication shape ceremony 59 caught in build-evidence-record. A semantic-support heuristic (keyword overlap between each sourced row's claim text and its cited records) was run over all 434 rows to hunt for further instances of that pattern; it returned only this one true positive, the rest being the repo's normal low-overlap 'consequence of X' writing style. Two further low-severity restatements found in cap-policy (best_practices[6], contract.shapes[1]) repeating agentic-stack/build-definition-of-done/cap-errors facts without naming them. Eight low-severity 'restate and extend' findings recorded across cap-identity, cap-isolation, cap-isolation-implement, cap-mandate-broker, cap-mandate-broker-implement, cap-memory-implement, cap-model-access and cap-model-access-implement, grouping the validator's per-skill restate-and-extend warnings (about 30 individual rows) by skill: each names its owning skill correctly for the restated fact but the trailing 'what this adds'/'consequence here' clause is an uncited extension not marked proposed. No description whose trigger clauses fail to fire on its skill's actual scope; no adapter row naming a product outside the Adapters section (validator: 0 hits across all 13); every second adapter differs in execution model from its first on multiple axes (confirmed live for 6 pairs via harness cross-adapter checks: 2-6 axes differing each), and cap-identity, the one skill with no adapters[] array, carries the required open question naming where its adapter pair lives instead. No definition_of_done found that cannot fail, and no measured_run found that contradicts its own breakage text.
